profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a for-profit public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, USA, trading as NVDA. Its website centers on the NVIDIA Nemotron family, which the company describes as highly efficient, multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents. The site says Nemotron models provide agentic reasoning for graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding, and are available as NVIDIA NIM microservices. It also mentions Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard, with support on NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark.

NVIDIA Nemotron is an enterprise LLM family with synthetic data generation, GPU optimization, and self-hosted options. NVIDIA NIM provides inference microservices for deploying foundation models, with enterprise GPU optimization and self-hosted options. The site describes the NVIDIA Open Model License as permissive, allowing use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA, and says NVIDIA publishes model weights, datasets, and training techniques. Tools mentioned include NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, NIM, SGLang, and vLLM.

For the fiscal period ended January 25, 2026, NVIDIA reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 in a 10-K filing. It files with the SEC under CIK 0001045810. NVIDIA is associated with 281 law exposure entries in California and no listed cases. The site includes comments from Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, and mentions ServiceNow's evaluation of Nemotron's visual Q&A accuracy.
